questionnaires.title: Thinking Patterns Worksheet (CPT)
questionnaires.description: A CPT worksheet for identifying unhelpful patterns of thinking in a trauma-related thought. For each pattern the client checks whether it fits and describes how it affects them.

items.text: Listed below are patterns of thinking that often become automatic, habitual thoughts and lead us into self-defeating behaviour. Write down a thought related to your trauma, then for each pattern check whether it fits that thought and how it affects you. A thought can fit more than one pattern, and that is fine.
Jumping to conclusions or predicting the future — does this pattern fit the thought? If so, how does it affect you?
Ignoring important parts of a situation — does this pattern fit the thought? If so, how does it affect you?
Oversimplifying things as “good–bad” or “right–wrong,” or overreaching from a single incident — does this pattern fit the thought? If so, how does it affect you?
Mind reading (assuming that people are thinking negatively of you when there is no definitive evidence of this) — does this pattern fit the thought? If so, how does it affect you?
Emotional reasoning (using your emotions as proof — e.g., “I feel fear, so I must be in danger”) — does this pattern fit the thought? If so, how does it affect you?
